correctness.rationale: For n>k>2 every q-subset except the n complements of consecutive k-arcs is a possible facet of the cut complex, and the lower (q-2)-skeleton agrees with the full simplex skeleton. Bayer et al. Theorem 27 establishes shellability, hence vanishing H~_(q-2). The pair long exact sequence yields the canonical surjection from the skeleton top homology, naturally wedge^q of augmentation lattice U_n, onto the oriented missing-face permutation lattice. The reflection s(i)=k-1-i fixes the representative omitted face, acts there by epsilon_q=(-1)^((q-1)/2). For odd n and even k, its unique fixed vertex v lies in missing facet F; R=F\{v} is reflection-invariant and every other extension of R is by an s-paired vertex of B. Any invariant mod2 cycle lifting the F-coordinate 1 would have boundary coefficient 1 at R, contradiction. Therefore no mod2 D_n-section; an integral section would reduce to one. Independent finite parity cases n=7,9,11 are consistent but the full statement follows from the invariant-face argument.
correctness.risk: Non-splitting is for this canonical integral equivariant exact sequence, not an assertion that any conceivable abstract module decomposition is impossible.
